extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers practicing practical criticism / close reading of poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reading, judging, and writing critical responses to lyric poetry, emphasizing close attention to technique (rhythm, rhyme, diction, imagery) and the relation of form to meaning and emotion. Intended to train readers to distinguish sincere poetic effect from stock responses, sentimentality, and technical mannerisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique (alliteration, internal rhyme, double rhyme)
rubrics_metrics.description: The technique in particular is very good. One notices particularly the alliterations, e.g. “Wild weeds that are rank with the rains.” Again, the double rhyme in the last line but one is very effective: it suddenly makes the thing more cheerful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific sound devices (alliteration, internal rhymes, double rhyme) and note their emotional or tonal effect; cite examples in the poem where a technique changes mood or emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: One also notices the way in which various details are symbolical. The “rains” suggest tears, to take only one example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify concrete details that carry symbolic suggestion; show how these contribute to overall meaning rather than being merely decorative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: Of course, by the emotion in it that one must judge a poem. The emotion in this poem is strong and sincere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish genuine feeling from cheap or manufactured emotion; give evidence of sincerity (depth, consistency, convincing particulars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical value vs jingling rhyme
rubrics_metrics.description: Has little meaning and no musical value. A mere jingling rime, in which words are chosen carelessly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether rhyme and sound create real musical value or merely a careless jingling; check word choice for subordination to sound vs sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diction and word-choice appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Words are chosen carelessly. ‘Life lies dead’ is nonsense. Too many unaccentuated short words; hence slurring necessary in reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether diction is precise and appropriate to tone; note when awkward or careless phrasing undermines meaning or requires unnatural delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antithesis and contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: The antithetical effects are well achieved; the repetition of “weeds” in the third verse is an excellent touch... The third verse contains a flood of pathos, emphasized by an admirable contrast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out effective oppositions (spring/winter, roses/weeds) and how they heighten pathos or argument; note when antithesis is too easy and undermines feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition and internal rhyming as structural touches
rubrics_metrics.description: The repetition of ‘weeds’ in the third verse is an excellent touch, as is the internal riming in the third line of the fourth verse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention repetition and internal rhyme when they reinforce theme or movement; explain their structural contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythmic swing, lilt, and cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: The poem has a swing and lilt to it which make it delightful reading. Pleasing melancholy because it gives one the safe 'luxury of grief' second-hand. Rhythm so pleasing that I have read and re-read solely for that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe overall rhythmic effect (swing, lilt, cadence) and its readerly appeal; note whether rhythm supports or contradicts meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentimentality vs genuine feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Few things are more disgusting than cheap emotion expressed in easy tears... Without sincerity poetry is an impossibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag cheap sentiment, cant phrases, and obvious rhymes as markers of sentimentality; require evidence that feeling is earned rather than manufactured by formal devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of treatment to subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject is serious but the treatment childishly and forcedly simple and they don’t fit in with each other. It has degenerated into mere sentimentality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether technique/tone fits the seriousness or simplicity of the subject; mismatch is a flaw (serious content with flippant technique, or vice versa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective versus personal association influences
rubrics_metrics.description: I have a special personal association with regard to this composition which might pre-dispose me in its favour. My judgement however is that it is thoroughly bad... The personal association, the mnemonic irrelevance, might be expected to threaten this poem to an especial degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge and bracket personal associations; attempt objective appraisal rather than allowing private memories or stock responses to dominate judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meter and metrical suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: The metre employed suggests doggerel and the worst kind of limerick... Possibly this is suggested by the metre, which is to a certain extent dactylic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse metrical pattern and how it suggests voice, register, or genre; note when metre produces unintended comic or trivial effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation of rhythm and sound to meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Perfect adaptation of rhythm and sound to meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise when rhythm/sound align with semantic content; criticize when sound undermines sense or emotional aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and intelligibility of sense
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere sense of this poem baffled an unusually large number of readers... Since the hyperbole of this particular beauty as God’s memorial is worked in twice... a full comprehension of it is necessary to the reading of the poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether comprehension of the poem’s propositional content is necessary for its effect; if so, assess clarity and argumentation; if not, consider other kinds where incoherence may be tolerable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of poem: argument vs mood vs irrationality
rubrics_metrics.description: There are types of poetry... where the argument, the interconnection of the thought, has very little to do with the proper effect... There are other types where the effect may turn upon irrationality...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify the poem’s mode: didactic/argumentative, mood-based, or intentionally irrational; judge by appropriate standards for that mode rather than one universal rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-idea fit (e.g., sonnet expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sonnet form is peculiarly felicitous because a very definite form is thus used for a very definite idea... The thought evidently ought to be a splendid one, if it is to accord with the manner of the sonnet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider genre/formal expectations (sonnet, lyric) and whether the poem’s idea warrants or matches the chosen form; mismatch may indicate failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of remembered comparisons (stock responses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons may have a positive or a negative effect... Sometimes the other poetry that is recalled assists the reader... But equally often these recollections... are a stumbling-block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note when recall of other poets aids interpretation or when it causes inappropriate bias; avoid letting reputation of other works substitute for close reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of doctrine and explicit beliefs in poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctrinal problem, the place and importance of beliefs in poetry, is in need of discussion... If poetry only expresses a 'state of mind' or 'mood', the thoughts presented need not be examined on their own account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about doctrinal or religious assertions in poems; decide whether to treat such statements as propositional claims or as part of a mood, and judge accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone authenticity and suspicion of pose
rubrics_metrics.description: The style is not quite genuine I feel from the continual change... There is a rather suspicious disclaimer... a pose assumed for the writing of the sonnet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect self-consciousness or theatrical posing; prefer work that convinces as authentic rather than staged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and aptness of metaphor and imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: The metaphors are apt, and although not complicated, they carry such a train of suggestions... The images are conventional and unconvincing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate metaphors for freshness, aptness, and associative power; conventional or clumsy metaphors weaken effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of language simplicity vs expressive power
rubrics_metrics.description: The simplicity of this poem contrasts with the empty-headedness of 2. Here ordinary words and images are used to celebrate the most elemental passion... The poem is simple in language and this simplicity tends to mask the thought any way in the first reading but adds to the effect when the poem is more closely studied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether simple language suits the poem’s aims and whether it conveys depth or merely masks emptiness; consider first impressions and effects of closer study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader response distribution and pedagogical implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Of 62 who returned protocols, 17 declare themselves bewildered; 14 appear to have fathomed it... These figures would suggest that the poem really is extraordinarily obscure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use aggregated reader responses to diagnose obscurity, common misunderstandings, and teaching opportunities; observe patterns (bewilderment, superficial praise) as diagnostic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-impression vs sustained reading effects
rubrics_metrics.description: On first reading, without fitting together the whole grammatically, meaning and spirit is caught... But if it lacks limpidity, it does, by becoming something of a nut to crack, take on a 'tang'—an enticement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between immediate impressions and what emerges after repeated readings; note when obscurity is a deliberate enticement versus an actual flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound texture and phonetic detail (sibilance, monosyllables, long vowels)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a crescendo... the prevalence of 'S' sounds in it culminates in the quick monosyllables 'will not be lost.' The first lines with their long vowel sounds move slowly and melodiously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to phonetic shaping (sibilance, vowel length, monosyllables) and how they structure pace and intensity; connect these observations to emotional arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural economy and closing lines (ending evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The last two lines... 'Make known him Master, and for what good reason.' The last line, however, is disturbing to the extreme. Ugly and flat and banal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate closural lines for strength and appropriateness; weak or flat endings can mar otherwise successful poems—explain why the ending succeeds or fails.
